_comment: Zenodo deposit metadata template for the DSFB-GPU S-REAL.3 publishable bundle. Submit this JSON via the Zenodo REST API or paste-edit into the Zenodo web form when creating the record.
title: DSFB-GPU S-REAL Audit Gauntlet — 20 Real Public Datasets, 5 Source-Class Families, Byte-Identical Replay
description: DSFB-GPU is a deterministic CUDA inference engine for densorial / tekmeric inference on residual evidence streams. This Zenodo deposit packages the S-REAL audit gauntlet: 20 byte-identical-replay-verified deterministic audits over real public datasets across five source-class families (DebuggingSoftwareTelemetry, ObservabilityTraces, TimeSeriesAnomaly, ReliabilityIndustrial, SoftwareDefects). Every fixture is SHA-256-pinned; every projection recipe is byte-deterministic; every audit's final case-file hash is replay-verified on two consecutive dispatches. The deposit does NOT claim domain truth, detector superiority, causality, or commercial redistribution rights for datasets with no upstream license. It is a breadth-and-replayability proof.

related_identifiers._note: DSFB-Debug Structural Detector-Field Residual Semiotics Engine — original prior-art paper for the DSFB lineage.
TADBench TrainTicket microservice anomaly corpus (Steidl 2022). Four fixtures derived (F11, F04, F19, F11b).
LO2: Microservice Dataset of Logs and Metrics (Bakhtin et al. 2025). One fixture derived.

non_claims: DSFB-GPU does not assert which admitted episodes correspond to real-world anomalies, faults, defects, or causal events. The audit reports structural residual evidence only.
DSFB-GPU does not claim detector superiority over any other anomaly-detection method. The admitted-episode counts are structural evidence, not benchmark verdicts.

For NASA C-MAPSS datasets, DSFB-GPU does not predict remaining useful life. It deterministically projects a public run-to-failure trajectory into a residual evidence stream and emits replayable structural episodes whose timing and motif distribution are consistent with degradation-shaped dynamics.
For software-defect datasets, DSFB-GPU does not classify bug severity. Patch line counts and CK metrics are projection inputs; the audit reports structural outliers, not defect predictions.
Datasets tagged 'no-upstream-license' are redistributed under academic research-use convention. No commercial-redistribution right is asserted.
Byte-identical replay is asserted only for the recorded toolchain (RTX 4080 SUPER, CUDA 13.2). Cross-driver / cross-CUDA / cross-hardware byte-identity is not claimed.
